newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania inflation and trade deficit improve.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania inflation and trade deficit improve.

text.p: Tanzania's annual inflation rate fell to 14 percent in January from 15.4 percent in December and is expected to drop to 10 percent by June because of anti-inflationary fiscal and monetary policies, the Bank of Tanzania said on Friday in its monthly report.
The central bank also reported a sharp drop in the trade deficit in January, to $21.1 million, from $94.9 million in the corresponding month in 1996.

Exports rose to $100 million in January from $61.6 million in the same month last year, because of higher shipments of coffee, cotton, sisal, tea, tobacco and cashewnuts, while imports fell to $121.1 million from $156.5 million.
The January annual inflation rate compares to 25.1 percent for the year ended January 1996.

"In view of the current anti-inflationary monetary and fiscal policy measures being pursued by the bank and government, respectively, the inflation rate is expected to decline furthur to 10 percent by the end of June 1997," the report said.
However, prolonged drought and insufficient short rains are pushing up food prices.

"Food crop prices have started to increase, reflecting the scarcity of food grains in the market. The Food Security Department of the Ministry of Agriculture is currently planning to redistribute the food stocks in the Strategic Grain Reserve (SGR) to the open market to stabilise prices," the bank's report said.
At the end of January, Tanzania's total external debt stood at $7.638 billion.

Paris Club creditors in January granted Tanzania debt reduction involving cancellation of $1 billion and rescheduling of $700 million of debt. However, the final figure of debt relief will be established only after bilateral negotiations with creditor countries expected to be concluded by June 1997.
